chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Al-Minqari, from Isa ibn Yunus, from Al-Awzari, from Al-Zuhri, from Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said:
When you take a prisoner who is unable to walk and you have no carrier with you, then send him back and do not kill him, for you do not know what the ruling of the Imam is regarding him.
He said, and the prisoner said: When he becomes a Muslim, his blood is saved and he becomes booty (property of the Muslims).
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a prisoner who cannot walk and has no carrier?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Sajjad (AS) highlights the principle of *istishab* (presumption of innocence regarding status) in military jurisprudence, advising commanders to release incapacitated prisoners rather than execute them due to uncertainty about the Imam's final ruling. It further establishes the legal transition of a prisoner upon conversion, where their blood becomes inviolable (*huqinat damuh*) and they are incorporated into the communal spoils of war (*fa'i*), reflecting the Shia emphasis on mercy and procedural caution in governance.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Al Miqary, from Isa Bin Yunus, from Al Awzary, from al Zuhry, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>

having said: ‘Whenever you take a prisoner, so he is frustrated from the walking and there is no carrier with you, so send him (back home) and do not kill him, for you do not know what is the decision of the Imam<sup>asws</sup> regarding him’.
He (the narrator) said, ‘And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The prisoner, when he becomes a Muslim, so he has saved his blood and becomes one of us’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from af-Qasim ibn Muhammad from af-Minqariy from ‘Isa ibn Yunus al-Awza’iy from al-Zuhriy from Ali ibn al-Husayn, recipients of divine supreme covenant, who has said the following: “
If you take a prisoner who is not able to walk and you do not have a carriage to carry him, then allow him to go and do not kill him; you do not know what is the command of the Imam about him.’
The narrator has said that he (the Imam) then said, ‘If a prisoner becomes a Muslim, his life is spared and he is one of us.’”
